Level 1 rules:
- Usual player is a 4x4 diagonal block [14 14 / 0 0] over [0 0 / 14 14]; normal movement usually shifts 1 object slot (4 px).
- 8/13 behaves like portals; effect depends on entry direction/state.
- Original rightward chain: entering 8/13 from the left twice was safe and relocated; the next right-side 8/13 in that chain caused GAME_OVER.
- Entering 9/10 from the right is safe and relocates.
- On one 9/10 branch, moving up relocated and changed the top 14-band to 4s.
- Entering 8/13 from the right in an upper-right branch sent the player to a lower-left/central-12 layout; there one right was safe and the second right caused GAME_OVER.
- 9/10 from the right can also land near 7/6; entering 7/6 from the right appears safe and non-teleporting.
- After the 7/6 branch, moving up then entering 8/13 from the right eventually led to a duplicated/multi-block state after 9/10 from the left; active piece became ambiguous.
- In that duplicated state, select appears safe and cycles an underlying state / active copy, changing visible special blocks and lower border 4-columns; nonzero block color can switch (14/0 vs 12/0).
- Lower-left 12/0 candidate: left/up/right/down probes were inconclusive.
- Lower-left 14/0 branch: right from the 14/0 candidate toggled it into a solid 4x4 14 at the same spot; up from the solid 14 changed it back into diagonal 14/0; another up from that diagonal caused GAME_OVER. So that lower-left 14/0 branch is stateful and dangerous.
- After reset, repeated rights from the visually identical start appear to move hiddenly along the route.
- Enough hidden rights from reset eventually produced a visible far-right 14/0 candidate immediately left of 8/13, supporting a hidden-right route.
- Moving right from that far-right visible 14/0 into 8/13 from the left leads back into the duplicated or multi-block state with multiple 14/0 and 12 blocks, making the active piece ambiguous again.
- Latest selects continue to change the arrangement without yet revealing a uniquely controllable active piece.
- Best probe in the ambiguous state remained safe select rather than movement until a clear repeat or controllable state appeared.
- Movement probes from the visible central 12/0 candidate (up/right/left/down) showed no obvious visible effect, so that 12/0 is likely inactive or not the active copy.
- New lower-right branch seems to mirror the lower-left one horizontally: left from the lower-right diagonal 14/0 turned it into a solid 4x4 14, and up from that solid restored the diagonal 14/0 in the same area.
- Right from that restored lower-right diagonal produced no obvious visible change.
- Critical new hazard: down from that restored lower-right diagonal caused GAME_OVER. This likely mirrors the lower-left branch's dangerous extra-up behavior under horizontal reflection.
- Reset is required after that branch. After reset, best to resume the previously mapped safer opening/hidden-right route rather than continue this dangerous mirrored branch immediately.
- Hidden-right progression can resurface a visible multi-structure layout with 12/0 blocks and lower-right 14/0 again; when that happens, treat it as the ambiguous select-cycle state and prefer select over arbitrary movement.
- Current resurfaced layout again matches that ambiguous state, so resume safe select cycling here.
- Another select still does not reveal a uniquely identifiable controllable copy; continue preferring safe select while the arrangement keeps cycling.

Playfield has a decorative border; the diagonal 14/0 tile is usually the controllable piece. Directional moves through empty floor shift it one coarse step. Entering adjacent 8/13 causes major relocation/state changes, so 8/13 is likely portal/swap. Tile 12 is not a simple push block: horizontal entry often places the player on the opposite side while 12 stays put, acting like cross-through/swap. Interacting with 7/6 while adjacent triggers large state changes; in normal mode it can relocate the diagonal player into a post-7/6 state. In that post-7/6 state, repeated right moves seem linked to distant 12 motion, suggesting remote control. Entering adjacent 12 from that state caused a global transformation: the bottom 14 band became 11 and the player became harder to locate. In the transformed 11-band state, left can re-expose the diagonal player near lower-right 12; right into 12 hides it again. Selecting beside 12 changed the local cluster into solid 14 plus split 12/0. Transformed mode supports ordinary horizontal movement of the visible 14/0 cluster. Selecting on 7/6 in transformed mode caused a second-stage transformation: the bottom band changed from 11 to 8, the local area by 7/6 became solid 14, and a new far-right 12/0 pattern appeared. Repeated selects on 7/6 in this later transformed state seem to pull that 12/0 structure leftward into the local area while shrinking the remaining distant decorative band, producing a progression like 7/6 -> 14/0 -> 12. Selecting 7/6 can also revert to the earlier visible post-7/6 mode, restoring the local diagonal 14/0 cluster. In that restored visible mode, repeated right moves can cause remote global changes even when the local 14/0 cluster does not obviously move: top decorative 14 patches convert to 4, the large bottom 14 band shrinks from the right, and the visible 14/0 cluster can reappear farther right in repeated lanes near the checker edge. Best current probe is still to keep testing right until a threshold, border interaction, relocation, or portal-style trigger finally appears. Latest evidence: the repeated right pattern is still active, so continue right until it clearly stops or produces a new state change.

Level 1 summary:
- 0/14 checkers move on a coarse 4-cell grid over 5-floor.
- 9/10: from one tile left, right pulls 9/10 left into contact; another right from contact removes it and updates indicators.
- 8/13: from one tile left, right triggers relocation/reconfiguration instead of 9/10 behavior.
- Fatal: left from direct contact on the right side of 8/13 causes GAME_OVER.
- Safe local rule: if checker is directly right of 8/13 with open floor on its right, move right to disengage.
- 8/13 can shift top 14-groups and the 12 block; altered layouts persist across reset.
- Multiple visible checker copies can exist; select may cycle active control invisibly. After using select once, a following right caused GAME_OVER, so use select cautiously.
- Contact with shifted 12 may recolor/fuse with checker rather than merely block (12/0 hybrid evidence).
- Broad floor probes can change layout even when active control is uncertain.
- Broad right probes in ambiguity-heavy multi-checker states can also cause GAME_OVER; horizontal probes are dangerous when control is unclear.
- 7/6 has a nonfatal mirrored two-step interaction: left from one tile right of 7/6 safely enters right-side contact; another left shifts checker to the left side and changes distant 0/14 indicators.
- Repeated resets can still leave multiple visible 0/14 copies because altered layouts persist; reset does not guarantee a unique visible active checker.
- Working safety heuristic in ambiguity-heavy states: prefer vertical probes over left/right.
- Latest vertical-probe behavior: up/down are nonfatal and can reposition mid-board and lower-area 14/0 inserts, and sometimes the 12 block.
- Recent pattern suggests these vertical probes may be cycling among board phases rather than producing steady progress, but they are still safer than horizontal ambiguity probes.
- Likely phase cycle: a lower 14/0-by-7/6 phase and a corridor phase with 14/0 inserted between the left 9/10 pair and the nearby 8/13 pair.
- New observation: right from the unique corridor sandwich/contact state was nonfatal and caused a large global reconfiguration: top-left 14 groups changed, the 12 block shifted to the right-side lower-mid area, and multiple visible 14/0 inserts appeared again, so control is ambiguous.
- Current plan: return to the vertical-probe safety heuristic; next test is up.
